mechanisms.name: Unit-store inflight admission gate (max_inflight_units)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: client_task select! disables the offer arm while store.len() ≥ max_inflight_units → offers stay in the mpsc → QueueFull propagates to the app once the channel also fills. Store shrinks only on first-ACK (runtime.rs:1157) or RECOVERED (runtime.rs:1130).
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product uses the default 4096 (kama_product.rs:147-231 does not override max_inflight_units). Never reached at the campaign msg counts.
mechanisms.telemetry: Indirect only: ClientStats.undelivered (= store.len() at drain end, runtime.rs:1382). No counter for "admission stalled".
mechanisms.notes: The bound is unit-COUNT, not bytes; spec §14 states the pool bound in BYTES (TX_POOL_MAX bytes). With max_unit_bytes=1200 the implied cap is ~4.9 MB, unstated anywhere.

mechanisms.name: Unit identity assignment (unit_id, u64 monotonic, offer-order-bound)
spec_refs: specs/kama-noise-wire-tdd-v2.0.md:370 §2.6 ID-SCOPE/WRAP (block_id session+direction-scoped monoton u32, NO-REUSE; message_id ...)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: offer arm → per-chunk `id = next_unit; next_unit += 1` (runtime.rs:1229) → store.insert(id, body) → drive!(Event::AppData(OpaqueUnit{id,size})) → wire header carries unit_id u64 BE (wire.rs:22 encode_data / wire.rs:65 encode_data_frag) → receiver admit_chunk dedups on it (runtime.rs:1694).
mechanisms.default_state: always on; starts at 0 per client_task
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product relies on it structurally: `unit_id = warmup_msgs + msg_id` (kama_product.rs:245-247, 534) — the bench declares a run INVALID if any offer is skipped, because msg-index↔unit_id is a 1:1 assumption.
mechanisms.telemetry: Delivery.unit_id (runtime.rs:606) and the acked() stream carry it; KP-CLIENT does not print ids.
evidence: crates/client-core/src/wire.rs:22 `pub fn encode_data(seq: u16, unit_id: u64, payload: &[u8])`
mechanisms.notes: unit_id is NOT the spec's message_id: in fragmented mode message_id is a separate u32 counter (runtime.rs:890) and unit_id numbers chunks. FEC block/esi are derived arithmetically from unit_id (runtime.rs:2183-2184), so unit_id is load-bearing for FEC alignment on BOTH ends.

mechanisms.notes: Receiver reconstructs against its own largest_seq+1 (its rx view); sender reconstructs the ACK's largest against max_emitted_seq+1. Both are ±32768 windows. FEC repair shards also consume wire seq (runtime.rs:998, 1004) — the seq space is shared across DATA/retx/dup/FEC but NOT with CS_PROBE (separate namespace, sender.rs:3207-3210).

mechanisms.bench_exposure: exercised in every kama-product run.
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.acked (runtime.rs:470) — NOT printed by KP-CLIENT; only the derived `delivered=` count (bench computes it from the acked() stream, kama_product.rs:527-540).

Pruning happens only on ACK/RECOVERED — a unit that is retransmitted many times and never acked accumulates one seq_to_unit entry per emission with no independent cap (see open questions).

mechanisms.name: First-ACK-wins delivery confirmation (sender-side delivery accounting)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: UDP recv → seam.open → AckFrame::decode → acked_full(max_emitted_seq+1) → per seq → seq_to_unit → store.remove(unit).is_some() (the idempotence latch) → stats.acked++ → unit_acked! → acked_tx.try_send(unit) → app ClientHandle::acked(). Separately the raw acked_seqs vector is fed diff-free into Event::AckReceived(AckInfo) (runtime.rs:1166-1172).
mechanisms.default_state: always on; acked channel depth = max(offer_queue, max_inflight_units) (runtime.rs:714)
mechanisms.activation_condition: any ACK frame (0x10 or 0x14) that opens and decodes
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product's entire completion metric is this stream: `a = cli.acked()` → delivered_ns[i] (kama_product.rs:527-540).
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.acked; bench RawEvent.delivered_ns (event.rs:17).
mechanisms.notes: MEASUREMENT SEMANTICS: bench `delivered_ns` is the SENDER's ACK-arrival timestamp, not the receiver's delivery timestamp. "Completion" in every kama-product run is therefore delivery-confirmation-at-sender, which includes the reverse-path RTT. The receiver-side delivery count exists only as ServerStats.delivered, printed in KP-SERVER.

mechanisms.name: Message-level ACK aggregation (fragmented mode: msg_pending / messages_acked)
spec_refs: specs/kama-noise-wire-tdd-v2.0.md:364 §2.6 canonical source prefix (message_id, chunk_offset, source_flags final/end-of-message)
specs/signaling-seam-v0.md:41 §3 delivery semantiği (deadline-bounded reliable; "ulaştı" = peer aldı)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: offer arm → if frag_on: msg_pending[msg_id] = n_chunks, unit_msg[chunk_id] = msg_id → ACK or RECOVERED → unit_acked!(unit) → unit_msg.remove → decrement msg_pending → at 0: stats.messages_acked++ and acked_tx.try_send(msg_id). ACK and FEC-RECOVERED share this single point (runtime.rs:1133 and 1159).
mechanisms.default_state: OFF — max_message_bytes: None (runtime.rs:186); messages_acked stays 0 and unit ids flow directly
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product turns it on IMPLICITLY whenever payload > FEC chunk capacity: `max_message_bytes: (payload > unit).then_some(payload)` (kama_product.rs:148). With --fec-profile 0 (FEC off) unit == payload → frag OFF. So the message-ACK path only runs in FEC arms with payload > E−11.
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.messages_acked (runtime.rs:513). NOT printed by KP-CLIENT.
mechanisms.feature_off_behavior: frag_on=false → the else branch sends the unit id straight through; identical to pre-fragmenter behaviour and wire-identical (0x00 DATA).
evidence: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1078-1084 `if let Some(m) = unit_msg.remove(&$unit) { ... if *rem == 0 { stats.messages_acked += 1; acked_tx.try_send(u64::from(m)) } }`
mechanisms.notes: In frag mode the acked() stream carries MESSAGE ids (0-based, one per offer) while in non-frag mode it carries UNIT ids. The bench's `unit.checked_sub(base_id)` works in both only because each offer produces exactly one message and warmup offers consume ids in the same counter.

mechanisms.name: Store-miss / stale-decision header-only emission
mechanisms.product_call_chain: drive! → decision for a unit whose store entry is gone (already acked by another copy) → emits a header-only frame anyway (so the engine's inflight accounting is not falsified) → stats.stale_decisions++ → seam → wire. Receiver dedups the unit and ACKs the seq.
mechanisms.activation_condition: engine plans a retransmit/duplicate for a unit already removed from the store
mechanisms.bench_exposure: printed by KP-CLIENT as `stale={}` (kama_product.rs:583).
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.stale_decisions — printed by KP-CLIENT.
mechanisms.duplicates_or_dead: Also incremented for unhandled decision kinds (runtime.rs:1021) — a FecParity decision when FEC is off. That second use makes the counter ambiguous.
evidence: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1026-1034 `let (payload, stale) = match store.get(&d.unit_id) { Some(p)=>(p.as_slice(),false), None=>(&[],true) }; if stale { stats.stale_decisions += 1; }`
mechanisms.notes: In fragmented mode a stale emission carries an ALL-ZERO 11-byte SourcePrefix (message_id=0, offset=0, len=0). The receiver decodes it, ACKs the seq, and inserts a zero-length chunk at offset 0 of message 0 (runtime.rs:1036-1043, 2157). This is documented as harmless (first-wins keeps a real chunk) but means a stale frame can seed msg_asm entry 0 on a peer that has never seen message 0.

mechanisms.name: Shutdown drain (pif→0 or drain_cap) + undelivered residue
spec_refs: specs/transport-layer-tdd.md:177 §4.2 Worst-Case Delivery Envelope (bounded store-and-forward teslim)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: ClientHandle::shutdown → watch(true) → main loop breaks → leftover offers counted (runtime.rs:1355) → drain loop: exits when store empty AND sender.diag_pif()==0, else at deadline = now + drain_cap → stats.undelivered = store.len().
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product sets `drain_cap: Duration::ZERO` (kama_product.rs:166) — the product drain is DISABLED in every benchmark run; the drain loop's sleep_until fires immediately.
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.undelivered, ClientStats.flow_end_ns (runtime.rs:1360). flow_end_ns IS printed (`flow_end=`, kama_product.rs:597); undelivered is not.
mechanisms.feature_off_behavior: drain_cap = 0 → no drain; residue reported as undelivered.
mechanisms.notes: flow_end_ns is stamped BEFORE the drain (runtime.rs:1360) so it is comparable with sender-internal timestamps. The bench's drain_cap=0 means no benchmark result has ever exercised the product drain path.

mechanisms.name: Unaccepted-offer accounting at shutdown
mechanisms.product_call_chain: main loop break → `while offer_rx.try_recv().is_ok() { stats.unaccepted_offers += 1 }`
mechanisms.bench_exposure: never triggered in kama-product (offer() blocks until accepted before shutdown).
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.unaccepted_offers — NOT printed by KP-CLIENT; asserted in tests (runtime_e2e.rs:220).

mechanisms.name: Receiver delivery channel — bounded try_send + delivery_dropped
mechanisms.product_call_chain: server_task recv → admit_chunk (runtime.rs:2157 DATA path / runtime.rs:1906 FEC-recovery path) → push_delivery → delivery_tx.try_send → stats.delivered++ (and fec_recovered_units++ if from_fec) else stats.delivery_dropped++ → app ServerHandle::next_delivery().
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product server_loop drains it in a select! and counts (kama_product.rs:353-359); uses the default 1024.
mechanisms.telemetry: ServerStats.delivered / delivery_dropped / fec_recovered_units — all inside the `stats={stats:?}` Debug print of KP-SERVER (kama_product.rs:379-381).
mechanisms.notes: A dropped delivery still marks the unit/message as delivered in delivered_seen (runtime.rs:1694/1729 run BEFORE push_delivery) — so an app that under-drains loses the payload permanently, with only a counter. Documented as "app drenaj sözleşmesi".

mechanisms.name: Receiver first-delivery dedup window (delivered_seen, DELIVERED_DEDUP_WINDOW)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: admit_chunk → non-frag: `if !slot.delivered_seen.insert(unit_id) { return }` then pop_first over 8192; frag: `if slot.delivered_seen.contains(&mid) { return }` … on completion insert(mid) + pop_first.
mechanisms.activation_condition: every arriving DATA/DATA_FRAG and every FEC-recovered chunk
mechanisms.bench_exposure: exercised in every kama-product run with retransmits.
mechanisms.telemetry: none — no counter for suppressed duplicate deliveries at this layer (only Receiver.was_duplicate internally, which the runtime discards).
mechanisms.duplicates_or_dead: Overlaps with Receiver's seq-level dedup (receiver.rs:221) but is NOT redundant: the doc at runtime.rs:1565 records that a retransmit carries a NEW seq, so the seq-dedup cannot catch unit repetition (26 duplicate deliveries were measured in the first netem gate run).
mechanisms.notes: pop_first on a BTreeSet evicts the numerically SMALLEST id, which equals "oldest" only while ids increase monotonically. message_id is u32 and wraps (runtime.rs:1220 wrapping_add) — after 2^32 messages the eviction order inverts. Documented in-code as "en-eski id düşer" which is an approximation, and the comment already concedes out-of-window very-late duplicates can be re-delivered (E2E envelope §4 is the final authority).

mechanisms.name: Receiver seq dedup + bounded rx-set (RX_DEDUP_WINDOW, RX_DUP_SUPPRESS)
spec_refs: specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:904 §14 (rx_reorder_pool ≤ RX_POOL_MAX; fazla out-of-order → en eski drop)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: server_task → slot.rx.on_datagram(RxDatagram{seq: full, unit_id, kind}) (runtime.rs:2148) → if received.contains(seq) → state=DupSuppress, forced ACK, delivered empty → runtime's `out.delivered.contains(&unit_id)` guard (runtime.rs:2156) skips admit_chunk.
mechanisms.default_state: always on, 4096 distinct seqs per peer
mechanisms.bench_exposure: exercised in every kama-product run.
mechanisms.telemetry: none exported to ServerStats; RxOutput.was_duplicate is dropped by the runtime (runtime.rs:2148 ignores it).
evidence: crates/adaptive-transport/src/receiver.rs:221-230 `if self.received.contains(&d.seq) { self.state = RxState::DupSuppress; let ack = self.tick_ack(now_ns, true); return RxOutput{ delivered: Vec::new(), ack, was_duplicate: true } }`

mechanisms.product_call_chain: app → ClientSender::send_with_deadline(payload, Some(ns)) → offer channel carries (Vec<u8>, Option<u64>) → offer arm: `if let Some(d) = deadline_ns { session.sender_mut().declare_delivery_deadline(d) }` (runtime.rs:1211) → Sender keeps the tightest → tightest_deadline_over_srtt() feeds FusionObservation.deadline_over_srtt_permille (sender.rs:3494) → FusionPolicy (only when cfg.fusion_policy is Some).

mechanisms.bench_exposure: only the `--fec-mode policy` arm: deadline_ns = Some(...) (kama_product.rs:429-432) and fusion_policy = calibration_v2_deadline (kama_product.rs:229-230). All other kama-product arms pass None.

The runtime never checks whether a message actually met its deadline; deadline attainment is computed off-line by crates/bench/src/metrics.rs:44 completion().

mechanisms.name: Production fragmenter — message → chunk split with canonical SourcePrefix (0x05 DATA_FRAG)

mechanisms.product_call_chain: offer arm → n_chunks = len.div_ceil(max_unit_bytes) → per chunk: SourcePrefix{message_id, chunk_offset, actual_payload_len, FINAL on last} → serialize_symbol into `body` (single canonical source) → store.insert(id, body) → drive!(AppData) → drive! emits encode_data_frag(seq, unit_id, body) (runtime.rs:1042) → seam → wire → server decode_data_frag (runtime.rs:2056) → admit_chunk with the wire-carried prefix.

mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product enables it implicitly when payload > FEC chunk capacity (kama_product.rs:145-149). Pinned by kama_product.rs:1063 `benchmark_payload_now_fragments_instead_of_being_refused`.
mechanisms.telemetry: ClientStats.frag_encode_failures (should be 0); ServerStats.frag_chunks_rx / msgs_reassembled / frag_chunk_dropped / msg_asm_evicted. None printed by KP-CLIENT; the server ones ride in KP-SERVER's `stats={stats:?}`.

mechanisms.name: Message reassembly (MsgAsm insert / take_if_complete, fail-closed on gaps)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: server recv → decode_data_frag / FEC reconstruct → admit_chunk(frag_on=true) → slot.msgs.entry(message_id).or_insert(MsgAsm::new) → insert(offset, payload, FINAL, cap) → take_if_complete() → Some(full) → delivered_seen.insert(mid), msgs_reassembled++, push_delivery(peer, mid, full).
mechanisms.activation_condition: fragmentation on and a chunk with the message's FINAL flag has arrived plus gapless coverage of 0..total_len
mechanisms.bench_exposure: exercised in the FEC arms whose payload exceeds the symbol capacity.
mechanisms.telemetry: ServerStats.msgs_reassembled / frag_chunks_rx (runtime.rs:582-585) — in KP-SERVER's Debug dump only.
mechanisms.feature_off_behavior: the msgs map is never touched
evidence: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1637-1650 `fn take_if_complete(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> { let total = self.total_len?; ... if off as usize != out.len() { return None; } ... (out.len() == total).then_some(out) }`
mechanisms.notes: take_if_complete is fail-closed on gaps AND on overlaps (offset != running length). Duplicate offsets are first-wins (runtime.rs:1626). A chunk arriving from FEC reconstruction and one arriving over the wire are indistinguishable here — that is the §11 forward-recovery join at the message layer.

mechanisms.name: msg_asm eviction (MSG_ASM_CAP, bounded half-message buffer)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: admit_chunk frag branch → message not complete → `else if slot.msgs.len() > MSG_ASM_CAP { slot.msgs.pop_first(); stats.msg_asm_evicted += 1; }`
mechanisms.gate: RuntimeConfig::max_message_bytes (only fills when fragmentation is on)
mechanisms.default_state: OFF (fragmentation off); cap is a hard-coded 64 half-messages per peer, not configurable
mechanisms.activation_condition: more than 64 simultaneously incomplete messages from one peer
mechanisms.bench_exposure: kama-product offers messages sequentially; the cap is not approached in any campaign configuration.
mechanisms.telemetry: ServerStats.msg_asm_evicted — present in KP-SERVER's Debug dump. NEVER asserted by any test (only destructured in api_surface_v0.rs:214).
evidence: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1584-1586 `/// [S1B] Peer-başına aynı anda birleştirilen mesaj tavanı ... const MSG_ASM_CAP: usize = 64;`
crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:1735-1738 `} else if slot.msgs.len() > MSG_ASM_CAP { slot.msgs.pop_first(); stats.msg_asm_evicted += 1; }`
mechanisms.notes: Two caveats. (1) `pop_first()` on BTreeMap<u32, MsgAsm> evicts the LOWEST message_id, not the oldest arrival — correct only while ids increase and only pre-wrap (message_id wraps, runtime.rs:1220). (2) The eviction check runs ONLY in the not-complete branch, so a burst of completions cannot trim an over-cap map in the same call. Untested: confidence medium because the behaviour is never asserted anywhere.

mechanisms.name: Per-message byte bound before allocation (frag_chunk_dropped)
spec_refs: specs/transport-layer-tdd.md:748 PARSER-02 (untrusted length ile asla with_capacity; bounds-check alloc'tan önce)
mechanisms.product_call_chain: admit_chunk → MsgAsm::insert → rejects if offset+len > max_message_bytes, or if cumulative buffered > cap → returns false → stats.frag_chunk_dropped++.
mechanisms.activation_condition: a malicious/corrupt FINAL or offset that would push the reassembly over the app cap

open_questions: No product binary exists. `[[bin]]` appears only in crates/bench/Cargo.toml:28. The only non-test callers of ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint are crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs and crates/client-core/examples/{p1_endpoint,fec_arm_compare}.rs. Whether 'PRODUCT PATH' means the library surface alone, or requires a shipping binary, is a scoping decision I could not settle from the specs.

seq_to_unit growth bound: entries are inserted per emission (runtime.rs:975) and pruned only when the unit is ACKed or RECOVERED (runtime.rs:1160, 1136). A unit that is retransmitted indefinitely without ever being acknowledged accumulates one map entry per emission with no independent cap. Whether ARQ/tail-recovery bound the retransmit count per unit is a sender.rs question I did not resolve (tail probes are bounded by max_tail_probes, but §9 selective retransmit budget was not audited in this cluster).

Bench does NOT run product defaults for two RuntimeConfig fields, so no benchmark result reflects RuntimeConfig::default(): `structure_gate_level_permille: gate` (kama_product.rs:229) is None unless --gate-permille is passed, overriding the product default Some(250); and `fec_loss_risk` is FecLossRiskConfig::default() unless --fec-risk (kama_product.rs:186-190), overriding the product default bounded_v1(). Both are FEC-cluster settings, but they mean 'the bench exercises the product runtime' is true only up to these two overrides. Also `drain_cap: Duration::ZERO` (kama_product.rs:166) disables the product drain in every run.

IdentitySeam's tag is exactly 16 B, which is also the engine's assumption in BS_PROBE_WIRE_EXACT=44 (28 B body + 16 B tag). I could not determine whether any code enforces `seam.sealed_len(LEN_CS_PROBE) == BS_PROBE_WIRE_EXACT`; if a future seam's overhead differs, the engine's cold-start byte budget silently decouples from the wire. No test pins this.

engine-spec §3.3-A [K-D2] normatively requires the PreConverge burst to be clamped to ONE unit; the shipped default initial_window_bytes = DEFAULT_BURST_CAP (2×MTU) deliberately restores a multi-packet first flight, justified in-code by an n=6/cell netem measurement (runtime.rs:117-140). Whether this is an approved spec amendment or an unrecorded deviation is not resolvable from specs/ — I found no amendment text for it.

engine-spec §3.3-B states 'Kopyalar da AYNI pacer'dan geçer (§13); pacer'ı baypas eden gönderim yolu YOK'. DR-EST-1's drain_establish_probe is explicitly token-exempt (sender.rs:1385-1390 'token'sız kol', sender.rs:2497-2498). Since establish_probe is default-ON in the product, this is a live, default-on violation of a NORMATİF sentence unless an amendment exists that I did not find.

CS_ECHO responder rate-limit: engine §11.1(iii) and noise-wire §2.57 ('rate-limit T_ECHO_MIN/akış') both require one; I found no throttle anywhere in the product path. Whether a [CAL] value was ever chosen for T_ECHO_MIN is unknown — grep for T_ECHO_MIN in crates/ returns nothing.

Whether the 8192-entry delivered_seen window and 4096-entry rx dedup window are adequate at the campaign's message rates was not computed. Both use pop_first (numerically-smallest eviction) which is 'oldest' only pre-wrap; message_id is u32 with wrapping_add (runtime.rs:1220). No test covers wrap behaviour.

ServerStats has no per-class tx byte split (the client's TxClass has five classes; the server's srv_seal_send has none). §4.4.4 asks for ACK overhead as a required secondary metric; on the reverse path ACK, RECOVERED, PARAM_ACK and CS_ECHO bytes are indistinguishable. I could not find any place where reverse-path ACK overhead is actually computed from product runs.
